reasoning: Observing a patient and acting on a change happens at the bedside, while charting and reporting are done at the chart or computer. The instructions say to split an activity that is partly physical and partly at a computer, which Y does.

The target names three activities: assessing needs, planning or modifying care, and implementing interventions. Y leaves out implementation, which the target names explicitly. X codes all three, with assessment and implementation as bedside PHYSICAL work and planning as a DISCRETE care-plan contribution.

'Conferring with other team members as necessary' is a means of completing the evaluation, not a separate deliverable. Under the do-not-split rule for alternative means, Y's single DISCRETE evaluation is correct.

Routine tests that LPNs run, such as glucose sticks and urine dipsticks, are hands-on handling of samples and devices away from a computer, so PHYSICAL fits better than DISCRETE. Y codes both specimen collection and testing as PHYSICAL.
Preparing and examining trays are two routes to the same result, a tray that conforms to the prescribed diet, and both are hands-on. X's single PHYSICAL part is sufficient.
Making beds is part of readying a patient room, and both are the same kind of hands-on housekeeping, so splitting adds nothing. Y's single PHYSICAL part is adequate.
Counting stock is hands-on work in the supply room, while the requisition is a DISCRETE submission made at a computer or on a form. The physical-versus-computer split rule favours X.

Medical and personal care, household work such as cooking and tidying, and comforting the patient and teaching the family are three different activities. Y splits all three; X folds the household work into nursing care.

Following Example D, appointments are made both live and from written requests, and record-keeping is a separate activity from other clerical work. X has no part for appointments made from written requests and lumps everything else into a vague batch. Y's split follows the instructions more closely.
